SmoothLevel

past the square root for cycles built from small wheels
Planned: citation of a published resultring 2Primes in the columns of large cycles: level of distribution and Elliott-Halberstam

Restrict the widths in LevelOfDistribution to cycles built only from wheels below a small power of the largest number (the RNS cycles, divisors of the primorial modulus). For these the level is known past one half: Zhang reached one half plus 1/584, Polymath one half plus 7/300, and Stadlmann one half plus 1/40, then 0.5253. These are Zhang-type estimates; they need the cycles to split into factors of chosen sizes (DenseDivisibility) and are the input to Zhang's bounded gaps. Cited, not proved: the proofs rest on Kloosterman sums and Deligne's bounds, which are outside the RNS.

Published sources

  • Y. Zhang, Bounded gaps between primes, Ann. of Math. 179 (2014), 1121-1174 — level one half plus 1/584 for smooth widths, and bounded gaps from it; cited as zhang_smooth_level and smooth_level_bounded_gaps
  • D. H. J. Polymath, New equidistribution estimates of Zhang type, Algebra & Number Theory 8 (2014), arXiv 1402.0811 — level one half plus 7/300 for densely divisible smooth widths; cited as polymath_smooth_level
  • J. Stadlmann, On primes in arithmetic progressions and bounded gaps between many primes, arXiv 2309.00425 — level one half plus 1/40 for smooth widths
  • R. Li, Primes in arithmetic progressions to smooth moduli: a minorant version, arXiv 2505.09629 — records Stadlmann's further improvement to 0.5253 as the current best in this direction; the value cited as stadlmann_smooth_level (find Stadlmann's own source before citing)
